speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are here for a scalp and forehead rash. To help me understand what you are experiencing, how long have you had these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis.

The history of a 3-month-old infant with a red, scaly rash that appears or worsens in cold weather, combined with a family history of psoriasis, is highly suggestive of this common condition. I will not order further tests as the clinical presentation is classic, but I will monitor the rash to ensure it does not become infected or spread significantly.
